## Interactive Showcase: Watch TinyGPT Learn to Code

In Milestone 05, you train **TinyGPT** from scratch on the **TinyPy** and **TinyC** datasets. Watch the model progress from initial noise to 100% syntactically valid code verified by the Python AST compiler in under 40 seconds on a standard CPU:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Epoch 1: Random Character Babble

At initialization, the model outputs unstructured character sequences. Loss is high (~2.15) and delimiters fail to balance:

```text
╭───────────────── Prompt: def add(a, b): | FAIL (Syntax Error) ────────────────╮
│   1 def add(a, b):                                                           │
│   2     8x_q? #&^; return (;;                                                │
│   3     whiluf   seseselure                                                  │
╰────── SyntaxError: unexpected EOF while parsing in 14.1ms (temp=0.4) ────────╯
```

**Diagnostic**: Underfitting. The model has not yet learned character transitions or Python scoping syntax.

### Epoch 5: Syntax Scaffolding Emerges

By the midpoint, training loss drops to ~0.40. Keywords (`def`, `return`, `if`) and 4-space indentation lock into place:

```text
╭───────────────── Prompt: def add(a, b): | PASS (AST Valid) ──────────────────╮
│   1 def add(a, b):                                                           │
│   2     return a + b                                                         │
│   3     pass                                                                 │
╰──────── Valid AST (trimmed trailing line) in 18.2ms (temp=0.4, top_k=5) ─────╯
```

**Diagnostic**: Attention heads bind opening delimiters to closing statements with valid block scoping.

### Epoch 10: 100% AST Syntactic Validity

At convergence (loss ~0.18, perplexity 1.2), the model achieves 100% AST pass rate across benchmark prompts with live character typewriter streaming:

```text
╭───────────────── Prompt: def add(a, b): | PASS (AST Valid) ──────────────────╮
│   1 def add(a, b):                                                           │
│   2     return a + b                                                         │
╰──────────── Valid AST (exact parse) in 8.6ms (temp=0.4, top_k=5) ────────────╯
╭────────────────── Prompt: def relu(x): | PASS (AST Valid) ───────────────────╮
│   1 def relu(x):                                                             │
│   2     if x > 0:                                                            │
│   3         return x                                                         │
│   4     return 0                                                             │
╰─────────── Valid AST (exact parse) in 11.9ms (temp=0.4, top_k=5) ────────────╯
```

**Diagnostic**: 🏆 Milestone Achieved! Full generative autoregression running on student-authored autograd and attention layers.

:::

<div style="background: #f8fafc; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 0.5rem; padding: 1.25rem; margin: 1.5rem 0; text-align: center;">

## Why Build Instead of Use?

```{=html}
<p style="text-align: center; font-size: 1.3rem; font-style: italic; color: #475569; margin: 0 0 1.5rem 0; max-width: 600px; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;">
"Building systems creates irreversible understanding."
</p>
```

:::: {.comparison-grid}

::: {.comparison-bad}
[Traditional ML Education]{.comparison-title}

```python
import torch
model = torch.nn.Linear(784, 10)
output = model(input)
# When this breaks, you're stuck
```

**Problem**: You can't debug what you don't understand.
:::

::: {.comparison-good}
[TinyTorch: Build → Use → Reflect]{.comparison-title}

```python
# BUILD it yourself
class Linear:
    def forward(self, x):
        return x @ self.weight + self.bias

# USE it on real data
loss.backward()  # YOUR autograd
```

**Advantage**: You can debug it because you built it.
:::

::::
